title: Assessing Collagen and Elastin Pressure-dependent Microarchitectures in Live, Human Resistance Arteries by Label-free Fluorescence Microscopy
protocol: Collect tissue samples immediately upon excision during surgery.
Transfer the collected tissues to 4°C HEPES buffered physiological salt solution (HBS) immediately.
Store the collected tissues in HBS overnight at 4°C to wash out anesthetics.
Isolate resistance-sized arteries using sharp-tip forceps and micro-dissection scissors.
Mount isolated arteries in a pressure myograph for further study.
Mount glass cannulae with tip diameters of ~80 µm on cannulae holders.
Position the tips approximately 150 µm above the chamber glass bottom.
Fill both inlet and outlet tubing with HBS containing 1% BSA.
Connect the tubing to the pressure system.
Mount the isolated artery using two double knot sutures per cannula.
Hold the artery gently at one end using two pairs of sharp tip forceps.
Open the lumen of the artery and slide it onto the cannula.
Secure the artery on the cannula using two knots.
Apply a pressure of 5 mmHg to flush the lumen with HBS / 1% BSA.
Cannulate the other end of the artery and secure it on the cannula using two double knots.
Transfer the myograph to the microscope stage.
Pressurize the artery to 5 mmHg (inlet pressure = outlet pressure).
Heat the setup to 37 °C for 30 min.
Perform Experiment: Imaging of Arterial Diameter, Wall Thickness and Collagen and Elastin Microarchitecture Using TPEM
Quickly scan the cannulated artery pressurized to 5 mmHg using a 20X objective (numerical aperture (NA) ≥ 0.8) and low power excitation light.
Activate Mai Tai two-photon laser and set it to 820 nm excitation light.
Collect emission simultaneously in two channels.
Split emission light between the photomultipliers using a 460 nm long pass dichroic mirror.
Collect emission using 30-60 nm wide bandpass filters centered at 520 nm (elastin) and 410 nm (collagen), respectively.
Enable continuous scanning with 10 µs laser dwell time/pixel and 512 × 512 pixels for 100% field of view.
Manually scan through the artery to determine the depth where maximum diameter is observed.
Choose a rectangular slice covering the artery's widest diameter.
Scan a single frame with pixel size ≤ 300 nm/pixel.
Use as low excitation light power and pixel dwell time as possible to avoid photodamaging the live artery.
Obtain a rectangular image, e.g., 100 × 1024 pixels.
Save the image for later analyses.
Determine lumen diameter by drawing a line between the two internal elastic laminae at each side of the arterial lumen using Fiji software.
Measure wall thickness by drawing additional lines and clicking ctrl + M in Fiji.
Load the image in Fiji.
Set the scale by clicking Main menu | Analyze | set scale and enter µm/pixel and pixel ratio (1:1).
Save the measurements.
Image collagen and elastin microarchitecture at 5 mmHg.
Scan the entire thickness of the arterial wall to obtain 3D image stacks with good quality for 1-3 regions of interest along the length of the artery.
Obtain image stacks through the entire wall of the artery using a 60X objective, NA ≥ 1, optimized pixel sizes and z-spacing.
Calculate the optimal imaging conditions using the Scientific Volume Imaging Nyquist calculator.
Define z-stack start and end depth based on vessel wall thickness.
Set z-step spacing according to the calculated pixel density.
Perform the z-scan with defined parameters.
Save each channel separately from the z-scan.
Determine arterial diameter, wall thickness, and microarchitecture at 10 mmHg pressure.
Repeat steps for imaging conditions calculation and data collection at 20 mmHg pressure.
Repeat steps for imaging conditions calculation and data collection at 40 mmHg pressure.
Repeat steps for pressures 60, 80, and 100 mmHg.
Replace the buffer in the myograph chamber with fresh 37 °C HBS after each pressure step.
Allow the artery to adapt for 5 min prior to imaging following each change in pressure.
Apply 10 μM U46619 in the myograph chamber followed by addition of 10 μM bradykinin when a stable constriction is observed.
Record diameter and wall thickness after application of each compound.
Add 3 μM sodium nitroprusside when the artery is not fully dilated following addition of bradykinin and record diameter and wall thickness.
Add 4% formaldehyde in 1x phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) at 37 °C for 1 hour.
Wash the fixed artery three times in 1x PBS.
Gently slide the artery off the cannulae, touching only the parts outside the knots.
Store the artery in 1x PBS / 0.05 % sodium azide at 4 °C until imaging for elastin and collagen volume densities or other purposes.
Open image stack in Fiji.
Go to file | open image to choose the image stack.
Go to Image | stacks | z project… to choose the images and "Max Intensity Projection".
Save the max intensity projection as TIFF.
Choose as many IEL fiber branching points as possible using the "angle tool".
Click ctrl + M to measure each angle.
Open image stack in Fiji.
Go to File | Open Image to choose image stack.
Set the scale by going to Analyze | Set Scale and entering pixel dimensions.
Create a max intensity projection by going to Image | Stacks | Z Project…, choosing images, and selecting "Max Intensity Projection".
Change Image type to 8 bit TIFF by clicking Image | Type | 8 Bit and save the max intensity projection as TIFF.
Open the NeuronJ plugin by clicking Fiji | Plugins | Neuron J.
Open the 8-bit TIFF in NeuronJ by clicking Load Image | Select File.
Click Add Tracings, and select fibers to analyze by clicking on start and end of each fiber.
Click Measure Tracings, choose display tracing (Lf) and vertex measurements in the dialog box.
Copy and paste Fiji Neuron J tracings and vertices output to excel (or similar).
Calculate L0 using Pythagoras's theorem from the vertex measurements.
Calculate L0/Lf in Excel (or similar) and save the results.
Wash the artery once in PBS.
Stain the artery for 15 min in 1 µM eosin in 1x PBS in the dark.
Wash the artery three times in 1x PBS.
Place two pieces of double adhesive tape 1-1.5 cm apart on an object glass.
Apply one or more layers of tape to match the diameter of the artery to be mounted.
Place 10-20 µL of PBS on the glass in the middle of the square and place the artery in the PBS drop.
Place the coverslip on double adhesive tape.
Press the coverslip onto the tape.
Fill the reservoir between the coverslip and object glass with 1x PBS.
Refill the reservoir every hour to avoid drying of the sample.
Obtain image-stacks for collagen and elastin volume densities using a 20X objective with NA > 1.
Use a water immersion objective for imaging of fixed arteries under a coverslip.
Use a water dipping objective for imaging of vital arteries.
Ensure the coverslip matches the objective if it does not have a correction collar.
Calculate optimal pixel sizes and z-spacing using the Nyquist Calculator.
Alternatively, use a minimum pixel size of 300 nm and z-spacing of 1 µm.
Obtain three images along the length of the artery to determine intra-assay variability.
Image elastin using 820 nm excitation light and collect emission using a 30-60 nm wide bandpass filter centered at 520 nm.
Image collagen using 990 nm excitation light to avoid any excitation of elastin and other autofluorescent proteins.
Collect emission using 10-30 nm wide bandpass filter centered at 495 nm.
Save image stacks from each channel separately as TIFF files.
Convert TIFF image stacks to HDF5 using Fiji.
Create two data file folders on the computer hard drive, one for elastin and one for collagen image stacks, respectively.
Copy relevant image stacks to the respective folder.
Create two new Ilastik projects in the Ilastik software, one for elastin and one for collagen.
Open Ilastik | Create new project | pixel classification | new project | add data and select image folder created in step 8.2.
Import one 3D image stack to train the software.
Select the Input Data applet | main workspace area | Raw Data tab | Add new … | Add separate Image(s) and choose the desired image data.
Choose relevant features in the software.
Open Feature Selection applet | Select Feature which opens a new dialog.
Add at least two labels using the Add Label button under the Training applet.
Draw labels on top of the raw image stack using the paint brush styled annotation tool.
Select the appropriate label: click brush tool and start drawing.
Prompt Ilastik to analyze the image stack and look for similar features by clicking Enable Live Update.
Check carefully the prediction map.
Select the Thresholding applet in Ilastik.
Choose an appropriate method for thresholding.
Input label, smooth, threshold, and size filter parameters.
Click Apply to apply the threshold.
Frequently switch between Training and Segmentation applets during re-training.
Repeat the training of Ilastik until only elastin or collagen is recognized.
Select batch prediction input selection in Ilastik.
Add relevant image files for batch analysis.
Verify the results by visually comparing image masks with raw images.
Optimize the Ilastik mask.
Re-analyze any image stacks with unsatisfactory results.
Calculate elastin and collagen volume densities from Ilastik image masks using MATLAB.
Open MATLAB.
Select folder with ilastik image masks in MATLAB "current folder" window.
Copy the MATLAB script from Supplementary File 1 to the MATLAB editor and save as volumeCalculator.m.
Enter pixel sizes and pixel height in the script lines.
Save the script.
Go to MATLAB command window and enter "volumeCalculator('path-to-data')".
Click enter.
Each image mask is summed up and multiplied by the known pixel/voxel volume.
The output from MATLAB is the total volume of elastin and collagen in each image stack.
Save the results.
